title: The naive framing: "does taste keep it consistent?"
text: Someone assumed Claude keeps a design system consistent using taste. It doesn't, a written file does. So, does Claude use it skill.md to keep a design system consistent? A skill is a folder

title: A skill is a folder
text: Claude reads before it works. This one is called design system. It skill.md holds the full instruction set in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it then acts on it. The file is the program. The pipeline lives in the step section.

title: Read then execute
text: Claude reads each step in order then executes it linear, no branching unless a step says otherwise.

title: One file, one job
text: This skill has exactly one job, audit, document, or extend a design system checking for naming inconsistencies or hard coded values across components, writing documentation for components variants, states, and accessibility notes, or designing a new pattern that fits the system already there. title: Carry-out
text: New look. It checks your components against the patterns already in your code base and matches or extends what is already there.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, paste this into Claude. Audit my design system for naming inconsistencies and hard coded values. Walk me through your plan before you act. That last clause matters. Explaining the plan first surfaces the real constraint logic, not just a recommendation. Match not invented. Lay
